statement: Cut personal and company tax, align the company rate with the top personal rate, and lower GST to 12.5%

summary.why: The party says lower taxes improve compliance and investment and that New Zealand's rates should be no higher than Australia's.
summary.how: Also tackle public debt; a 2025 release calls for a 'flat tax rate' for individuals and companies.

statement: Stop taxing NZ Super (including for over-65s still working) and boarders' income in private homes

summary.how: Remove NZ Super from taxable income, and exempt genuine home-sharing/boarder income with safeguards against commercial use.

statement: Let mayors become full-time council CEOs and give ministers power to appoint and sack senior public servants

summary.why: The party says unelected bureaucrats and advisers usurp the mandate of elected representatives.
summary.how: Elected representatives at local and national level would get wide powers to dismiss obstructive or incompetent staff; legislate to curtail 'unconstitutional bureaucratic power'.

sources.title: Has New Zealand Lost Control of Its Own Government?

statement: Make cutting hospital waiting times the top health priority, funded from bureaucracy, procurement and productivity savings

summary.why: The party says the key issue is whether patients are treated in time, not how much is spent.
summary.how: Measure waits for elective surgery, specialists, diagnostics, cancer and ED; buy private capacity where it is quicker and competitive; grow the domestic workforce; link any extra funding to measurable results.

statement: Tighten immigration toward skilled migrants and cap other net migration by the supply of housing, doctors and school places

summary.why: The party says population growing faster than 'social goods' makes everyone poorer.
summary.how: A stable points system; end 'golden' investor visas; NZ licence tests for foreign truck drivers; tougher document checks and audits; report GDP per capita.

statement: Hold a Royal Commission of Inquiry into police under-performance and corruption

summary.why: The party cites fabricated drink-drive tests and lost public trust.
summary.how: Also: refer prima facie criminal allegations against police and all deaths caused by police action to the courts; protect identities of police witnesses in international drug cases; review drone laws.

sources.title: Announcement: Police Policy - Commission Of Inquiry Into Under Performance And Corruption

statement: Strengthen the IPCA: double its staff, quadruple its budget, and let it prosecute and name officers

summary.how: As set out in its 'Sharpening the Teeth of the IPCA' statement.

sources.title: Law & Justice Policy Statement: Sharpening the Teeth of the IPCA

statement: Improve access to justice for self-represented litigants

summary.how: Procedural changes, support services, legal aid reform, tax deductions and cost awards for pro bono work, and wider Family Dispute Resolution.

sources.title: Improving Access to Justice for Self-Represented Litigants

statement: Leave the Paris Agreement, scrap the ETS and repeal all 'climate'-based taxes, laws and agencies

summary.why: The party says there is no climate emergency and that climate policies raise food and energy costs and hurt the poor most.
summary.how: Remove fossil-fuel taxes and restrictions, abolish climate units in government, end energy subsidies of any kind, and stop public funding of methane research such as AgriZero.

statement: Oppose converting farmland to carbon forestry and oppose the Gene Technology Bill

summary.how: No incentives for permanent carbon forestry on productive land; keep restrictions on GMO field trials and release; revisit the Planning and Natural Environment Bills to make them workable and protect property rights.

sources.title: Policy clarification on rural, environmental, and agricultural issues

statement: Encourage oil and gas exploration with a Norway-style resource joint venture and sovereign investment fund

summary.why: The party says New Zealand has failed to secure a fair share of its resources.
summary.how: Public-private resource partnerships, royalties shared with local communities, environmental bonds, returns held in a New Zealand Investment Fund.

statement: Buy a fleet of oil tankers and build new oil refineries for fuel security

summary.how: Tankers would guarantee supply and floating storage until refineries able to process local and Pacific crude are built; also bring back manufacturing.

statement: Ensure 'cheap, reliable and abundant' energy without relying solely on solar and wind

summary.how: Renewables have a role but cannot be relied on alone because of variability.

statement: Create a Kermadec Ocean Sanctuary and overhaul fisheries management with cameras on all commercial vessels

summary.why: The party says the sustainable fisheries regime is widely abused.
summary.how: Promote the Kermadec Ocean Sanctuary Bill and reinstall surveillance cameras on commercial vessels.

sources.title: Has New Zealand Failed Its Oceans? Conservative Party Says Yes - Environment Policy update

statement: Increase penalties for child sexual offending and online exploitation

summary.how: Longer sentences for serious and repeat offenders, review of sentence reductions, better monitoring after release, more online-exploitation investigation resources and victim support.

statement: Restrict irreversible gender-related medical procedures for minors and require parental involvement

summary.how: Independent assessment before significant intervention, evidence-based practice, parental involvement subject to safeguards, and independent review mechanisms.

statement: Recognise an unborn child as a legal person from the third trimester

summary.why: The party says every human life has inherent dignity.
summary.how: An Unborn Child (Legal Personhood and Rights) Act with a protected right to life, without criminalising pregnant women, plus a Pregnancy and Family Support Programme (support payment, housing security, support services, adoption options).

statement: Review all trade agreements and pursue a neutral foreign policy with a support- and reconstruction-focused military

summary.how: Seek a balance between free trade and protectionism ('Trade before War'); avoid being drawn into conflicts that do not threaten NZ territory.

statement: Employment and services based on merit, 'one law for all', and 'a man is a man, and a woman is a woman'

summary.why: The party opposes policies that divide people by race, ancestry, sex or identity.
summary.how: Listed among its 'policies that work' alongside limiting unskilled immigration and defending free speech and Judeo-Christian traditions.
